_readme: The Castilian, 2323 San Antonio St, as js/slopes-apartments.js draws it. One 1969 slab: a full-site podium (retail ground floor, the parking garage behind a vertical metal fin screen, the level-11 amenity floor glazed dark) with the residential tower standing on its roof deck. Metres in the footprint's oriented bounding box (js/westcampus.js obbOf): L=77.0, W=36.9 as obbOf computes it (the ring itself is 77.45 x 36.86). u=0 is the NORTH end and +u runs SOUTH; v=0 is the WEST (San Antonio St) edge and +v runs EAST - confirmed against the console's frame line, see _frame_src. Every number carries a _src naming a key in `sources`, or says derived or unknown. Read docs/apartments.md for the schema.
name: The Castilian

sources.S1: data/snapshots/2026-08-27/buildings.detailed.geojson feature 307878e3-63d2-471c-83d1-6b405de9e7b7: name 'The Castilian', num_floors 22, final_height 60.0, source_height 'hero_override'; the footprint is a clean 4-vertex rectangle, 77.45 x 36.86 m (2,855 m2), long axis at bearing 184.9 deg.
sources.S2: sixthriver.com/castilian-1 (Sixthriver Architects, who did the 2015 $20M renovation for American Campus Communities): '22-Story High Rise', 344 units, originally constructed 1969, 11th floor is the amenity level - full-service kitchen and dining hall, study lounges, computer lab, laundry, gym.
sources.S3: educationsnapshots.com/projects/6742 (the same project, photographs by Casey Dunn): 22 floors; level 1 leasing office + retail; LEVELS 2-10 ARE THE PARKING GARAGE; level 11 amenities; levels 12-22 private rooms and shared suites.
sources.S4: educationsnapshots photograph 'american-campus-communities-the-castilian-1200x897' (ref/edusnap_00.jpg in the session scratchpad): the south-west corner in sun - the vertical metal fin screen over the garage, the dark navy glazed band at the top of the podium, the white spandrel band above the fins, the recessed dark ground floor under the podium overhang.
sources.S5: educationsnapshots photograph 'the-castilian-700x895' (ref/edusnap_02.jpg): the head-on San Antonio St elevation at the AMERICAN CAMPUS LEASING CENTER entrance, address plate 2323 - the fin screen at full resolution, the entrance canopy, the ground-floor storefront. Scale from a standing person, 1.7 m = 58 px -> 0.0293 m/px.
sources.S6: American Campus Communities gallery photograph 674-01-exterior-gallery (crop_tower.png in the session scratchpad; that copy is mirrored left-right, which does not move any measurement used here): the tower in sun, near head-on - the pale piers, the mid-grey spandrels, the dark glass, the charcoal core strip with the vertical CASTILIAN sign, the blank pale end wall with the ACC logo, the dark crown band under the parapet.
sources.S7: thedailytexan.com 2023 photograph 2-2-23_CastillianConditions_PeytonSims (ref/dailytexan_00.jpg): the east elevation from W 24th and Guadalupe under overcast - 11 window rows counted on the tower by a blueness profile at three columns, the amenity floor's dark glass band, the core strip and its sign on this face too.
sources.S8: Google Earth 3D, imagery 12/3/2023, captured 2026-09-05 with scripts/verify/chrome.mjs on hardware GL and page.screenshot(): nadir (camera 510 m, 30d17'14.31"N 97d44'32.67"W, scale bar 165 px = 30 m), obliques from the NW and the SW (328 m). The nadir was fitted in the building's own frame - a 10 m grid on the podium roof outline at 0.065 m per crop pixel - and every plan number below was read off that gridded plan with the roof-height parallax taken out (the tower roof stands 30 m above the podium roof and displaces radially outward by a factor 1.083).
sources.S9: scripts/bake_westcampus.py BUILDINGS['The Castilian'] and docs/PASS_WESTCAMPUS.md: 60.0 m, 22 storeys, 1967 (S2 says 1969), painted concrete with punched windows, base band 4.6 m, a garage podium, the amenity floor at 11 - the same programme S3 states, sourced independently.
sources.S10: docs/entrances/westcampus.md row 3: address 2323 San Antonio St, front elevation WEST on San Antonio (two OSM footway ends at 30.28769/30.28770), base band 4.60 m, retail suite + Castilian Cafe in the podium, the garage entry a ramp mouth on the west elevation.
sources.S11: js/westcampus.js SOLID trios, as The Standard's file uses them: the day/golden/night relationship for a deck and for a mechanical unit.
sources.derived: a number computed from the above and marked so; 'unknown' stays unknown.

footprint._src: S1 verbatim. In (u,v) the four corners are (0,0) (0,36.86) (77.45,36.86) (77.45,0) - the polygon IS its own oriented bounding box, so every edge is axis-parallel in the frame.

_frame_src: obbOf(ring) as the generator computes it, read off the boot console line: `[slopes-apartments] The Castilian: obb L=77.0 W=36.9, +u at bearing 184.9 deg`. +u runs SOUTH, so u=0 is the north end; +v is 90 deg counter-clockwise from +u in (east, north), i.e. EAST, so v=0 is the west (San Antonio St) edge. The ring measures 77.45 x 36.86 m corner to corner; the obb is 0.45 m shorter because it is fitted to the rotated hull.

levels._src: Total 60.0 m (S1/S9). The split is read off the SW oblique (S8) by measuring the three parts of the west elevation in one column: tower 355 px, amenity band 45 px, everything below 230 px, of 630 px total -> 33.8 / 4.3 / 21.9 m. The ground floor's 4.6 m is measured (S9/S10). The eleven tower floor lines are the eleven residential storeys (levels 12-22, S3), counted independently as eleven window rows in a blueness profile of the east elevation (S7) -> 2.9 m floor to floor, derived. The six garage deck lines between 4.6 and 21.0 are derived at 2.733 m: nine garage LEVELS are stated (S3), but only about six deck heights fit the measured 16.4 m, which is what a 1969 split-level ramp garage numbers as nine. Uncertainty: plus or minus one deck.
levels._heights_src: deck 25.6 + podium parapet 0.9 = 26.5; tower roof 58.6 + parapet 1.4 = 60.0 = S1's final_height. That 60.0 is a hero/LiDAR high point, and the mechanical penthouse stands above it (roofItems).

colours._src: day hex; golden and night follow js/westcampus.js's ramp() unless a full trio is given. Every hex is the median of a named crop of a named photograph.

pier._src: S6, median of the pier at (553,300)-(561,500) = #bcbebc and (730,300)-(736,500) = #b3b9b5 - the pale precast pier that runs the tower's full height

spandrel._src: S6, median of (690,349)-(720,357), the mid-grey spandrel between window rows inside one bay

glass._src: S6 measures the vision glass at #1b2936 in direct sun ((690,305)-(720,343)); S7 measures the same glass at #5a7582 under overcast, where it is reflecting the sky. The value entered is the midpoint of the two lighting conditions - derived from two measurements, not sampled once.

endPale._src: S6, median of the blank end wall at (1180,200)-(1250,600) = #ccd0d0, entered a step down because that crop is the sunlit face

core._src: S6, median of the charcoal core strip at (425,300)-(490,700) = #747972

crown._src: S6, median of the dark crown band under the parapet at (700,112)-(760,130) = #474643

sign._src: the white CASTILIAN sign panel (S6, S7, S8). S6's crop reads #a3a7a3 because that face is in shade; entered as the white it is.

finLight._src: S5, median of a lit fin face at (200,200)-(214,300)

finShade._src: S5, median of the shaded side of the same fins at (182,200)-(198,300) = #475372 and (216,200)-(222,300) = #576784

podiumWhite._src: S4, median of the white spandrel band above the fin screen at (860,600)-(1080,660)

amenityGlass._src: S7, median of the level-11 glazed band at (900,770)-(1120,800). In direct sun the same band reflects the sky and reads #3163b7 (S4) - the dark value is the material.

groundGlass._src: S5, median of the ground-floor storefront glazing at (240,660)-(300,780)

groundWall._src: S5, median of the dark panel beside the storefront at (540,660)-(600,760)

canopy._src: S5, median of the entrance canopy fascia at (60,620)-(500,640)

colours._roof_src: S8 nadir, median of the tower roof membrane at (660,560)-(720,640) = #ded7c7; golden and night entered the way S11 enters a top face
colours._deckTone_src: S8 nadir, medians of the two podium roof strips: #e0e0e0 west (in sun) and #a5aaad east (in the tower's shadow); the entered day value is between them, moved down one step after the first look, where a paler deck read as a bare cream plane against the reference's weathered concrete

penthouseWhite._src: S8: the mechanical penthouse reads as the brightest white on the roof in both obliques; entered between the roof membrane and the podium white, not separately sampled

coping._src: the parapet capping reads as the pale precast of the piers (S4/S6); not separately sampled

colours._condenser_src: S8 nadir: the roof units are mid grey; the trio is S11's mech tone, as The Standard's file uses it

skins._src: one rule per face treatment; every count comes from a module, never a hard-coded number

grid._src: The tower's long elevations. Bay 3.2 m: twenty pale piers were counted across one long face in a brightness profile of S6 at y 380-420 (piers at x 55, 81, 115, 151, 189, 228, 268, 310, 354, 400, then the core strip, then 499, 552, 607, 665, 726, 789, 857, 928, 1003, 1065), and eighteen in the same profile of the NW oblique (S8) - twenty bays plus the two-bay core strip across a 67 m tower face is 3.2 m. The pier is 0.9 m and the recessed channel between piers 2.3 m: a luminance profile across one bay of S6 (rows y 300-340, the bay from x 1002 to x 1065, 63 px) has the pier bright for 17 px - 27 % of the pitch - and the channel dark or mid-grey for the other 46. One window per bay per floor, 2.15 x 1.85 m on a 0.55 m sill: a vertical profile of the same photograph gives glass runs of 45 px in a 64 px floor pitch (70 %) and S7 gives 28 of 50 (56 %); 1.85 of 2.9 m is 64 %, between the two. The three tones keep the photograph's own order and roughly its spacing - measured luma 180 / 104 / 50 for pier / spandrel / glass, ours 189 / 110 / 65. The window reveal is the spandrel grey, not the pale coping: at the second look every window carried a white outline that no photograph has, and it was turning a dark glazed elevation into a pale one.

core._src: the charcoal lift and stair core strip that runs the tower's full height on both long faces, carrying the vertical sign (S6, S7, S8); also the dark crown band, which is the same tone

end._src: the tower's two end walls: blank pale precast with a single centred column of small stair-landing windows, one per floor, and the ACC logo near the top (S6's right-hand wall; both obliques, S8). Window size read off S8's south end at about 0.85 x 1.15 m, plus or minus 0.2 m.

fin._src: The garage screen: vertical metal fins over the whole podium above the ground floor. Pitch 0.57 m - 36 lit fin faces counted in a brightness profile of the head-on elevation (S5) across 700 px at S5's own scale, 0.0293 m/px, = 20.5 m. The lit face and the shaded side are about half the pitch each in S5 (lit runs 13-16 px, shaded 8-18 px, depending on each fin's angle to the sun). 0.20 m is below the low end of the shaded measurement, chosen deliberately: at this app's oblique camera the pitch is about two pixels, and a half-dark share turns the band into a moire barcode instead of the pale blue screen every photograph and the Google Earth mesh show. No window: the garage behind is open deck, and nothing reads through the screen in any photograph.

spandrelBand._src: the white band between the top of the fin screen and the amenity glazing (S4; both obliques, S8)

amenity._src: level 11, the amenity floor: a continuous dark glazed band on aluminium mullions round all four sides, under the deck parapet (S4, S7, S8). The 2.4 m mullion spacing is a plausible module read off S4's navy band - not dimensioned.

ground._src: level 1: leasing office, retail and the Castilian Cafe (S3, S10) behind a storefront that sits back under the podium overhang, with a white canopy fascia (S4, S5). Mullion 1.6 m read off S5 at its own scale. The recess itself is not modelled - the wall is in the podium plane; see `open`.

endPier._src: the podium's share of the tower's end wall: blank pale precast, no fins, no windows (S4, S8). Same tone as the tower's end walls above it, because it is the same wall.

penthouse._src: the mechanical penthouse walls (S8) - unused while the penthouse is a roofItem box, kept so a future block can wear it

blocks._src: The full site, ground to the roof deck: level 1 retail, the garage behind the fin screen, the white spandrel band, and the glazed amenity floor. All four faces wear the same stack - the fin screen and the dark band run right round in both obliques (S8) and in S4 and S7.
blocks._plan_src: the obb rectangle, not the ring: the footprint IS a rectangle (S1), and obbOf reports it as 77.0 x 36.9 against the ring's own 77.45 x 36.86, a 0.2 m difference at each end. It has to be entered as a rectangle rather than as `footprint` because clipWall only splits a wall it can prove is axis-parallel, and the ring's edges carry a fraction of a degree of numerical tilt; with the ring, the end-pier overrides below claimed the WHOLE end face and the podium lost its fin screen on both ends. That was the third look's finding.
blocks._parapet_src: the white upstand round the deck in both obliques (S8); 0.9 m is a look, sized to the band's own measured white edge

overrides._src: the north end: the tower's pale end wall does not stop at the deck, it runs to the ground as a blank pier with the fin screen returning against it on both sides (S4's right-hand volume; S8 SW, where the south pier is unmistakable below the deck line). Same width as the tower.

the south end, the same pier. This is the single clearest thing the second look found: the SW oblique shows a white wall running the full height at the middle of the south face, and the podium was drawing fin screen across it.

roofItems._src: S8 nadir: the east deck strip carries units along its whole length
S8 nadir: the west deck strip carries fewer, in two loose rows

blocks._src: The residential slab, levels 12-22 (S3). Plan read off the rectified nadir (S8) with the parallax taken out: v 8.6 to 23.6 (15.0 m deep - a double-loaded corridor), u 6.5 to 73.0, so the podium deck stands 8.6 m clear on the west, 13.3 m on the east, 6.5 m at the north end and 4 m at the south. The nadir's parallax correction put the north end at 7.5 and the south at 73, and the SW oblique shows a narrower deck strip at the south end than at the west, which is what those two numbers say. Plan uncertainty is plus or minus 3 m in u and 1.5 m in v.
blocks._bands_src: the punched grid to 57.0, then the dark crown band that stops the grid before the parapet (S6, S7) - `core` is that same charcoal. The band measures 0.93 m in S6 (18 px against a 56 px floor pitch) and is drawn 2.0 m: at the first look a 1.1 m band under a 1.4 m pale parapet vanished at the oblique camera, where the reference shows a clear dark line under the coping.

faces._src: u0 is the NORTH end wall and u1 the SOUTH: both blank pale precast with the stair-window column (S6, S8). v0 (west, San Antonio St) and v1 (east) take the default punched grid.

overrides._src: The lift and stair core: a charcoal strip the full height of both long faces, with the white vertical CASTILIAN sign panel on it. Position is 40 % of the tower's length from the north end - six bays stand north of it and ten to eleven south of it in the NW oblique's pier profile (S8), and it falls at the same fraction on the east face in S7. Width 6.4 m = two bays: the gap in S6's pier profile (411-499 px) is 1.76 times the local bay spacing and 2.0 times it in S8's. The sign panel is a white plate about 2.6 m wide - 40 % of the strip - hanging from just under the crown band and about 12 m tall, which is where S6 and S8 both put it; the letters are the same white, so `back` carries the plate and the dots stand proud of it.

roofItems._src: the lift overrun and mechanical penthouse, standing on the core: in the SW oblique it is a white box directly above the CASTILIAN strip, and in the NW oblique it sits 29-55 % of the tower's length from the north end - the core is at 40 %. It was first placed at the north end from the nadir alone, where the brightest block reads there once the parallax is taken out; the two obliques agree with each other and not with that, and a 64 m parallax correction on a 0.065 m/px plan is the weaker measurement, so the obliques win. 14 m long (19 % of the tower in the SW oblique) and 4.0 m tall against the tower parapet, plus or minus 2 m each.
S8 nadir: the two large round cooling-tower fans just south of the penthouse, about 3 m across (the renovation's new chiller and cooling tower, S3); drawn as a 2 x 2 of boxes so the cluster reads
S8 nadir: units scattered down the rest of the tower roof. Thinned from 8 x 3 after the third look, where a regular 24-box waffle covered a roof the reference keeps nearly clean.

open: The ground floor sits in the podium plane; in the photographs it is recessed about 2 m under the fin screen's overhang (S4, S5). The generator has no per-band inset, so it is drawn flush - a todo for the generator, or a second thin block.
The garage deck count is six, derived from the measured 16.4 m; the sources say nine LEVELS (S3), and a split-level ramp garage numbers half decks. A section or a garage plan would settle it.
The tower's setback at the two ends (about 5 m each) is the weakest number here: the nadir's parallax correction is the only evidence, and it disagreed with itself by 3 m between the two ends.

The fin screen is drawn as flat light and dark stripes, not as fins standing proud of the wall. At the oblique camera 0.57 m is about two pixels, and our frame shows moire arcs across the band that the reference does not have - any regular stripe at that pitch will. Lowering the dark share from 0.28 to 0.20 m softened it; only a coarser pitch or a texture would remove it, and both would be a worse answer than the measured one.
The garage ramp mouth on the west elevation (S10) and the entrance canopy (S5) are not drawn.
